name: Netanel (Son of Suar, leader from the tribe of Issachar)
title: Leader of the Tribe of Issachar
summary: Netanel, son of Suar, was the chosen leader and chief of the tribe of Issachar during the wilderness journey. He was appointed by God to assist Moses in the census at the Sinai desert, and he brought the tribe's offering at the dedication of the tabernacle. He represented the tribe of Issachar on all official occasions during the wilderness journey.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Leader of Issachar
keyEvents.description: God commanded Moses to appoint Nathanel, son of Zuar, as leader and representative of the tribe of Issachar during the census in the wilderness of Sinai.

keyEvents.title: The Census of the Tribe of Issachar
keyEvents.description: Under Nathanel's leadership, men from the tribe of Issachar aged twenty years and older were counted as 54,400 fighting men.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement Around the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Nathanel and the tribe of Issachar were assigned their place at Judah's camp on the east side of the tabernacle, along with Judah and Zebulun.

keyEvents.title: Offering at the Dedication of the Altar
keyEvents.description: Nathanel, son of Zuar, brought his offering on the second day during the dedication of the tabernacle's altar. His gift included a silver plate, a silver bowl, a gold spoon filled with incense, and various sacrificial animals.

keyEvents.title: Departure from Sinai
keyEvents.description: When the people of Israel broke camp from the wilderness of Sinai, the tribe of Issachar marched under Nathanel's leadership as part of Judah's division.
